While the 90% confidence intervals capture a wide range of probable outcomes, certain specific risks or "black swan" events could push actual results beyond these stated boundaries. For instance, a sudden and major shift in underlying conditions, such as an unexpected policy change, a significant technological breakthrough, or an abrupt external shock (like a natural disaster or an economic downturn), could invalidate the assumptions underpinning the forecast. Similarly, if the system being forecast is subject to critical thresholds, breaching one of these unexpectedly could trigger a cascade of effects, leading to an outcome dramatically higher or lower than even the outer bounds of the one-month interval.
